catalog.summary: Get connections — a connection record does not report which integrations use it
Get all integrations — the list view carries no `jobs`, so no connection references
Get integration by ID — the only op returning its connection references (`jobs[].sources[]`/`targets[].connectionId`)
Get an integration flow by ID

getConnections.description:
Minimum role: Restricted Integration User.

Retrieve all connections available to the authenticated user. Nothing in the returned record says whether a connection is referenced: determining that requires sweeping every integration with `getIntegrationById` and collecting `jobs[].sources[]`/`targets[].connectionId`.

status.description: Response envelope present on every successful CloudWorks operation.

body.description: Connection-type-specific fields. For AzureBlob includes `name`, `storageAccountName`, `containerName`, and `authMethod` (camelCase in response, contrasting with snake_case `auth_method` in create/update requests).

status.description: Connection health: 1 = active, 0 = error.

integrationErrorCode.description: Error code set when `status` is 0; null when the connection is healthy.

workspaceId.description: Anaplan workspace ID for restricted-user connections; null for unrestricted connections.

authMethod.description: Authentication method used by this connection (denormalized from `body.authMethod`). `"SAS-based"` for SAS-token connections; null for connections created before this field was introduced.

meta.description: Pagination metadata block returned with list responses.

tenantCurrentCount.description: Total number of integrations (including integration flows) in the tenant. Present in GET /integrations responses.

tenantMaxAllowed.description: Maximum number of integrations allowed for this tenant. Present in GET /integrations responses.

schema.description: URL to the JSON schema definition for this response type.

getIntegrations.description:
Minimum role: Restricted Integration User.

Retrieve all integrations. Returns 25 integrations if `offset` and `limit` are not provided.

Items are `IntegrationSummary`: no `jobs`, therefore no `connectionId` anywhere in the response. Mapping connections to integrations costs one `getIntegrationById` call per integration; there is no bulk form.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of items to skip. First element is 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of integrations to return.

parameters.name: myIntegrations
parameters.description: Scope of the returned list. Set to `1` to return only the current user's integrations. Omitted or set to `0` (the default), the response spans integrations owned by every user the caller can see — use this scoping when answering tenant-wide questions, such as which connections no integration references.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Sort field. Prefix with `-` for descending order. Example: `name` (ascending) or `-name` (descending).

getIntegrationById.description:
Minimum role: Restricted Integration User.

The only op that reveals which connections an integration uses: `integration.jobs[].sources[]` and `targets[]` carry `connectionId`. `getIntegrations` does not return `jobs`, so mapping connections to integrations costs one call per integration.

Imports bind the connection in `sources`, exports in `targets` — read both. `integrationType: "Process"` does not mean no connection: a process integration whose actions read from or write to the connected cloud data store carries `jobs` with `sources`/`targets` pointing at a connection, so a sweep must cover every integration type.
